# Artifact Keeper 1.9.1

A security patch release on the 1.9 line. Six fixes, no features, no schema change, no configuration change. Two of them change client-visible behaviour: credential exchanges are now capped at the presented credential's expiry (Conan/Docker clients using short-lived API tokens — read the first section), and logout now revokes the session's refresh tokens (see Security).

## Read this first — an exchanged session no longer outlives the credential that started it

Four endpoints took a presented credential and returned a fresh, **full-TTL** access JWT: the Conan `POST /conan/{repo}/v2/users/authenticate` exchange, and all three arms of the OCI `/v2/token` exchange — an API token supplied as the Basic password (`docker login`), a Bearer JWT swapped for a fresh one, and the keyless fallback that accepts a JWT as the Basic password.

Every one of them is chainable, because the JWT they mint is itself a credential those same endpoints accept. A holder of an API token expiring in five minutes could exchange it for a 30-minute bearer, swap that bearer for another just before each expiry, and keep access indefinitely without ever re-presenting the token. After the first exchange the credential's expiry bound nothing, and expiring or revoking it did not end the session it had started.

All four arms now cap the minted token at the presented credential's own expiry, so every chain is monotonically non-increasing and access dies with the credential that anchored it. The cap only ever narrows: a credential that outlives the configured access-token TTL still gets the full TTL, and a username/password login, which has no expiry, is unaffected.

**What you will see:** a Conan or Docker client authenticating with a short-lived API token is asked to re-authenticate when that token expires, rather than continuing on a self-renewing bearer. If a CI job relied on the old behaviour, give its token a lifetime that covers the job.

**Outstanding bearers are not revoked** and no audit record identifies them — but the chain is broken, so they expire within one access-token lifetime and cannot be renewed. If you suspect a specific credential of abuse, revoke it and force a password change on its owner.

**What is capped, exactly.** The Conan exchange and all three OCI `/v2/token` arms — every arm that mints from a presented credential. Not capped, because they mint from a real login rather than from an exchange: `/api/v1/auth/login` and the TOTP completion, `/api/v1/auth/refresh` (bounded by its own rotating refresh TTL and family revocation), and the OCI *offline* refresh token, which is only ever issued to a username/password login. One exchange surface stays uncapped on this line and on `main`: `POST /api/v1/ci/token`, which swaps a CI OIDC JWT for an AK bearer. It is not the same defect — the bearer it mints is not itself accepted as a CI OIDC assertion, so there is no renewal loop; obtaining another requires a fresh assertion from the CI provider.

The admin-configurable API token expiration policy this fix shipped alongside on `main` is **not** in 1.9.1; it ships in 1.10.0.

## Security

- **Credential exchange no longer mints a bearer that outlives the credential it was exchanged from** (#3817). An authentication bypass across four endpoints — the Conan authenticate exchange and all three OCI `/v2/token` arms. See above. Backported from the 1.10.0 work on #3460, without the policy feature.
- **The bundled `grype` scanner and the scanner-adapter's bundled `trivy` are rebuilt, clearing CVE-2026-84445** (#3815, #3790). CVE-2026-84445 (HIGH; gRPC-Go xDS servers crash on a request carrying neither `:authority` nor `Host`) was published on 2026-09-08 against the `google.golang.org/grpc` v1.83.1 that 1.9.0's images carry, and fails the release security gate on both images. Nothing in the source changed between the last green build and the first red one; the advisory did. The backend images move their grpc override one patch further, to v1.83.2, and the scanner-adapter is rebuilt on hardened trivy 0.74.0-r3 and published as 1.2.11. The vulnerable path is an xDS *server* and neither scanner serves anything, so the flaw was not reachable in Artifact Keeper; it is fixed rather than suppressed because a dependency CVE with a version to build against gets built.

- **SBOM mutation endpoints now require the repository write/delete action instead of read visibility** (#3826, GHSA-ww52-pmcg-f53c). Any read-only repository member — and on a public repository any authenticated user — could hard-delete an SBOM attestation, convert it to another format, or force a regeneration that deleted the existing document. Delete now requires the `delete` action and convert/generate require `write`, matching artifact writes. Behaviour change: non-members can no longer generate or convert SBOMs on public repositories, and members whose role lacks `delete` (e.g. `developer`) can no longer delete SBOMs.
- **Logout now actually revokes the session's refresh-token family** (#3826, GHSA-965p-gcgh-67vf). The revocation shipped in #1807 was never wired to the route, so a refresh token (7-day TTL) captured before logout remained fully usable afterward and no logout audit entry was written. Logout with a valid session now revokes the family server-side; anonymous logout is unchanged.
- **HuggingFace uploads reject filename path traversal at ingest** (#3826, GHSA-6wjw-gcvx-3q58). The `x-filename` header was spliced verbatim into the artifact path and storage key, so a writer of one model could overwrite any other file in the repository. Traversal filenames are now rejected (400), not sanitized.
- **All format write paths reject spec-invalid names, versions, and filenames at ingest** (#3826, GHSA-vcq6-8hxw-4q67). Terraform, cargo, helm, pypi, npm, goproxy, nuget, cran, composer, rubygems, jetbrains, conan, and ansible write paths accepted values containing `..`, `.`, `//`, backslashes, NULs, or percent-encoded variants and stored them verbatim. All now validate with the shared reject-at-ingest validator used by the generic REST upload.

## Upgrading

No migration, no configuration change, no API change beyond the capped `expires_in` a credential exchange reports. `1.9.1` is a drop-in replacement for `1.9.0`.

The scanner-adapter image ships as `1.2.11`. If you pin the adapter by exact version rather than by the floating `1.2` tag, move the pin.
